fields.features_heading: What the Agent Knows Before the First Showing
fields.features_subheading: A buyer answers once, on a phone, and the agent starts the first call knowing the budget, the deadline, and the deal-breakers.
fields.feature_1:
Questions that follow the buyer's situation

Ask whether the buyer owns a home now. A yes opens questions on whether it has to sell first and when it lists. A renter is asked when the lease ends instead, so nobody reads both.
fields.feature_2:
The preapproval letter, read into fields

Let buyers upload a preapproval letter. The form reads the lender, the amount, and the issue date into the buyer's record, and any value it cannot read goes to the agent to confirm.
fields.feature_3:
Must-haves kept apart from wish lists

Ask for bedrooms, parking, and the longest commute the buyer accepts as must-haves, then for a list of nice-to-haves. Search on the first list and use the second to break ties.
fields.feature_4:
Every buyer lands with one agent

Assign each buyer to the agent who covers the neighborhoods they picked, with the full answers in an email or a Slack message. Buyers on a tight move date reach that agent first.
fields.feature_5:
The buyer agreement on the last screen

Place your written buyer agreement after the final question and collect a typed or drawn signature. The signed copy is saved to the buyer's record with the date it was signed.
fields.feature_6:
Code your brokerage can keep

Export the full code of the form and its buyer database to your GitHub repository on paid plans. A developer can then connect it to the CRM or transaction software your office runs.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Kinds of Buyer, Four Next Steps
fields.tab_content_1:
When a buyer has no preapproval, a consult comes first

Dara Whitfield is buying her first home through Ansel Park Realty. She sets a budget of $425,000 and answers "Not yet" when the form asks about a preapproval letter. Any buyer without one is offered a 30-minute buyer consultation, and the showing request opens after it. Dara books the first open slot.
fields.tab_content_2:
Relocating in 45 days or less puts the agent on alert

Nadia Ferrer starts a new job in Columbus and has to move in 32 days. She tells Sorrel Bay Realty she can only tour by live video for now. Any move date within 45 days sends her agent, Calvin Shore, a Slack message with her answers. He lines up three video tours before the weekend.
fields.tab_content_3:
Any buyer with $800,000 or more goes to the luxury lead

Rookmere Realty splits the county between two area agents, and each buyer lands with the agent who covers them. A budget of $800,000 or more overrides the area and goes to Mei Lindqvist, the luxury lead. Of the four buyers who applied this morning, only Anouk Bell, at $950,000, is hers.
fields.tab_content_4:
All showings wait on a signed buyer agreement

The last screen at Willow Gate Realty is its written buyer agreement. An MLS participant working with a buyer has to sign one with that buyer before the first tour, so the form keeps the showing request locked until the signature is in. Marcus Quill reads the 90-day term, signs, and asks to see 14 Quince Lane.

plan.angle: The top 10 for this query is printables: Pinterest pins, Etsy and Canva templates at $7 to $10, a printable PDF and two blog templates. Each hands an agent a static list of questions. This page shows a buyer intake that acts on its answers: it books a consultation for buyers without a preapproval letter, flags relocations with a tight move date, assigns each buyer to the right agent on a team, and puts the written buyer agreement on the last screen so it is signed before the first tour.
tab_stories: A first-time buyer tells Ansel Park Realty she has no preapproval letter yet, so the form offers her a 30-minute buyer consultation before any showing request opens.
A buyer relocating for a new job enters a move date 32 days out, and because it falls within 45 days, Brookfield Realty's agent gets a Slack message and the buyer is offered live video tours.
Larkspur Realty's team intake reads each buyer's area and budget, sends each buyer to the agent who covers that area, and gives any budget of $800,000 or more to the luxury lead.

Willow Gate Realty ends its intake with the written buyer agreement, and the buyer's showing requests open only after she signs it, because MLS participants working with a buyer need that agreement before a tour.
